import json
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import pickle

# Fetch and parse the arXiv API response
response = web_fetch(
    url="http://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=multimodal+RAG&sortBy=submittedDate&sortOrder=descending&max_results=5",
    max_chars=10000
)

# Parse the XML content
root = ET.fromstring(response)
ns = {'atom': 'http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom'}

papers = []
for entry in root.findall('atom:entry', ns):
    paper = {
        'id': entry.find('atom:id', ns).text,
        'title': entry.find('atom:title', ns).text.strip(),
        'summary': entry.find('atom:summary', ns).text.strip(),
        'published': entry.find('atom:published', ns).text,
        'authors': [a.find('atom:name', ns).text for a in entry.findall('atom:author', ns)],
        'categories': [c.get('term') for c in entry.findall('atom:category', ns)],
        'link': next((l.get('href') for l in entry.findall('atom:link', ns) if l.get('rel') == 'alternate'), None)
    }
    papers.append(paper)

# Save for later use
with open('/tmp/papers.pkl', 'wb') as f:
    pickle.dump(papers, f)

print(f"Successfully fetched {len(papers)} papers.")
for i, p in enumerate(papers):
    print(f"{i+1}. {p['title']}")
    print(f"   Authors: {', '.join(p['authors'])}")
    print(f"   Summary: {p['summary'][:200]}...")
